title: Quotient of a regular ring by an element with a unit derivative is regular
statement: Let $R$ be a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], i.e. Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with $R_{\mathfrak p}$ a regular local ring for every prime $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $f\in R$ and let $D:R\to R$ be a derivation (an additive map with $D(ab)=aD(b)+bD(a)$) such that the image of $D(f)$ in $R/fR$ is a unit. Then $R/fR$ is a regular ring (if $f$ is a unit, $R/fR=0$, which has no primes and is regular).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PF (lemma-quotient-regular, line 11798) and its proof (reduction to R local; f not in m^2 by the Leibniz rule; Algebra Lemma Tag 00NQ lemma-regular-ring-CM)

proof.text: The quotient R/(f) is Noetherian. For every prime q of it let p be its inverse image in R. Then f belongs to p since its image in R/(f) is zero, and D(f) does not belong to p since its quotient image is a unit and q is proper. Thus f/1 belongs to the maximal ideal of R_p, while D(f)/1 is a unit there. If f is a unit, there are no q and the argument is vacuous.

Extend D to R_p using lem-weil-pbc-derivation-extends. Its value at f/1 is D(f)/1 and hence is a unit. By induction on sums of products of elements of the maximal ideal, additivity and Leibniz show that the derivative of every element of its square belongs to the maximal ideal: each product derivative is a sum of two terms each containing a factor in that ideal. Consequently f/1 is outside its square. Apply lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-hypersurface-criterion to conclude R_p/(f/1) is regular local.

proof.text: The extended ideal (f)R_p is the singleton span of f/1 by Ideal.map_span. Mathlib's quotient-localization instance identifies R_p/((f)R_p) as a localization of R/(f) at the image of p.primeCompl. Surjectivity of the quotient map identifies that submonoid with q.primeCompl. IsLocalization.algEquiv then identifies this regular local ring with Localization.AtPrime q. Transport regular localness along the ring equivalence and apply isRegularRing_iff.
